references.text: Washing of clothes as part of the cleansing process for someone who becomes unclean by touching something unclean.
The priest must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water as part of the cleansing ritual.
Washing of clothes and bathing in water as a cleansing ritual, with uncleanness lasting until evening.
The one who releases the goat for Azazel must wash his clothes and bathe his body before returning to the camp.
Washing of clothes and bathing before re-entering the camp, with uncleanness lasting until evening.
Uncleanness lasting until evening, after which the priest may eat from the holy offerings.
The same ritual applies to the one who burns the heifer: wash clothes, bathe, and remain unclean until evening.
The cleansing process includes washing of clothes and bathing; clean by evening.
The red heifer and the cleansing ritual point forward to Christ's blood that cleanses the conscience.
